'''''Erigeron coulteri''''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Asteraceae]] known by the common names '''large mountain fleabane''', '''Coulter's fleabane''', and '''Coulter's daisy'''.<ref>[https://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=3125 Calflora taxon report, University of California, ''Erigeron coulteri'' Porter. Coulter's Daisy,  Coulter's fleabane, large mountain fleabane ]</ref>

''Erigeron coulteri'' is native to much of the [[western United States]] where it grows in moist forests and meadows. It has been found in [[California]], [[Nevada]], [[Colorado]], [[New Mexico]], [[Wyoming]], [[Montana]], [[Oregon]], and [[Idaho]], though there are large stretches of land in between known populations.<ref>[https://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Erigeron%20coulteri.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref>

''Erigeron coulteri'' is a [[Perennial plant|perennial]] herb reaching maximum heights of 20-70 centimeters (8-28 inches). It has an erect stem which may have a few branches or none. There are leaves on its stem as well as at its base. The long leaves are somewhat [[Leaf shape|lance-shaped to more rounded]], and sometimes have a few teeth along the edges. The [[inflorescence]] atop the stem has one to four [[Head (botany)|flower heads]], each between one and two centimeters  (0.4-0.8 inches) wide. The center is packed with tiny golden yellow [[disc floret]]s and the circumference is fringed with up to 140 white [[ray florets]].<ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250066579 Flora of North America, ''Erigeron coulteri'' Porter 1874.  Coulter’s fleabane ]</ref>
